passive_load_exact_analysis.verdict: Candidate P (passive load, no reset) is FEASIBLE for ρ ∈ [0, 0.85]. At ρ=0 (R_S=0, my E-1 assumption), τ_off/τ_on=100; at ρ=0.85 (amplitude limit), τ_off/τ_on=1.2. Both exceed the required ratio 1.0. Candidate R (R-2 active reset) is needed only when ρ > 0.85 or when v_inf must be < 0.3 V but still drive a next-stage amplifier (not in this round).

E1_withdrawn: my E-1 '99x universal' assumed rho=0 (R_S=0), not general; v3 §3 corrects this
R2_note: With reset conductance k·(1/R_L) during the reset phase, τ_clear/(1+k) ≈ τ_settle. At ρ=0 (R_S=0), τ_off/τ_on=100, so k≈99 brings the ratio to ≈1. At ρ=0.85, the passive ratio is already 1.2, so k can be much smaller or zero.
R2_updated_ruling: R-2 active reset is OPTIONAL, not required. Use candidate P (passive, no reset) when rho <= 0.85; use candidate R (with reset) when rho > 0.85 or other constraints force it.
